description: Phase 9 Track A: production hardening per AUDIT.md (repo root — read it first; work follows its 'Recommended remediation order'). Six areas: (1) authn/authz/tenant isolation/safe errors, (2) atomic idempotent lifecycle execution, (3) post-settlement compensation saga, (4) fixed-precision monetary model, (5) key custody and approval minimization, (6) audit anchoring + defensive web controls + scalability. Constraints: never break the local demo flow (npm run setup && npm run dev must keep working end to end), keep all AGENTS.md invariants (state machine, append-only hash-chained audit, money types, per-network accounts, compliance fail-safe), and extend the vitest suite with every story.

All app/api route handlers use the helper for their catch paths; execute route no longer returns raw err.message or stack

userStories.notes: Done 2026-07-16. lib/api-errors.ts is framework-free (codes, status + canned-message tables, ApiError, apiError(), fromThrown(), SAFE_FAILURE_SUMMARY); the NextResponse wrappers live in app/api/guard.ts (errorResponse/invalidRequest/conflict/caughtErrorResponse), keeping the established 'HTTP concerns under app/api, lib/ stays vitest-callable' split. DECISION: unified EVERY error body to { error_code, message } rather than only the catch paths — the ACs list unauthorized/forbidden/not_found among the stable codes, and those come from guard, not a catch. That renamed the field the UI reads, so 3 client components moved from data.error to data.message (the login form hardcodes its own message and was unaffected), and ~19 test assertions changed. Deliberate message pass-through survives for errors a route CHOSE (validation strings, TreasuryError domain text); TreasuryError also keeps its specific `code` alongside `error_code` so the UI can still branch on a guardrail. Two extras beyond the ACs: POST /api/payments + /api/entities parsed JSON with no .catch, so a malformed body escaped as an unhandled 500 (now 400 invalid_request); and 'unknown sender_id or recipient_id' became a plain notFound() since it named which id was unknown. balances' 503 keeps its own shape (chain_unavailable) — the 'run npm run setup' hint IS the point of that response. Verified on a real dev server end to end: forced execute failure -> {payment_id, status:FAILED, error_code:execution_failed, message:'execution failed'} with the real 'Insufficient mockJPY liquidity... available 100000000' only in the server log; sender read failureReason as the safe summary, operator read the full detail; happy-path 25k USD->JPY still SETTLED; chain INTACT. Suite 176 -> 184.

userStories.title: Compare-and-swap status transitions
userStories.description: As a platform owner, I want every lifecycle transition to be conditional on the expected current status so that concurrent writers cannot corrupt state.
acceptanceCriteria: Executor setStatus (and any raw prisma.payment.update that changes status) becomes updateMany({ where: { id, status: expectedFrom }, data }) — zero rows updated throws a typed StaleTransitionError; assertTransition still runs first
The review and cancel routes use the same CAS path
DB test: two simulated concurrent transitions from the same status — exactly one wins, the loser gets StaleTransitionError and the payment ends in a single consistent status
Audit event is only written when the CAS update succeeded
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Done 2026-07-16 (5ac370d). New lib/transitions.ts is now the ONLY way a payment's status changes: transitionStatus(payment, to, {data, detail, action, actor}) runs assertTransition, then CASes with updateMany({where:{id, status: from}}) and audits only if count === 1. lib/state.ts stays pure (no prisma) so the unit layer keeps working; transitions imports db+audit+state, and executor/routes import transitions — no cycle. DECISION: StaleTransitionError extends ApiError('conflict') rather than following treasury's typed-code + per-route mapping precedent, because api-errors.ts explicitly exists for 'a lib that knows what the client should be told' — the payoff is that the routes' existing caughtErrorResponse renders the 409 with zero mapping code. Converted beyond the ACs: the execute route's compliance-gate updates (QUOTED->COMPLIANCE_PENDING->REJECTED/MANUAL_REVIEW/APPROVED) were raw updates, so two concurrent executes could both run (and bill for) compliance — AC1 says 'any raw prisma.payment.update that changes status', so they are in scope. GOTCHA found while converting the executor's catch: it used to raw-update FAILED->FAILED when the refund leg threw after the FAILED write landed; a legal-move assert now rejects that, so the catch returns early when payment.status is already FAILED. The `payment = {...payment, ...(await setStatus(...))}` assignments became load-bearing (they carry the CAS's expected value) — noted in AGENTS.md. Tests: tests/db/transitions.test.ts (5) + tests/integration/cas-routes.test.ts (2, racing reviewers and racing cancels through the real handlers). Suite 184 -> 191, tsc + lint green. No UI change, so no browser pass; the executor E2E integration tests exercise the converted path on the fixture chains.

userStories.title: Per-payment execution lease claimed atomically with liquidity reservation
userStories.description: As a platform owner, I want double-execution to be impossible: one lease per payment, claimed in the same DB transaction that reserves liquidity.
acceptanceCriteria: Payment gets executionLeaseId + leasedAt columns; execute claims the lease with a CAS update (WHERE id = ? AND executionLeaseId IS NULL AND status = 'APPROVED') inside the same prisma.$transaction that creates the LiquidityReservation
Second concurrent execute returns 409 conflict (error_code conflict) without touching chain state
Lease is cleared on terminal states (SETTLED/FAILED/REFUNDED/COMPENSATED) so operator retries stay possible where the state machine allows
Integration test: fire two executes concurrently at one APPROVED payment on the local fixture chains — exactly one settles, the other 409s, exactly one escrow tx exists on-chain
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Done 2026-07-16. Payment gains executionLeaseId + leasedAt; executePayment claims the lease with a CAS (where {id, status:'APPROVED', executionLeaseId:null}) as its first write, then runs the existing body via a new runExecution() helper wrapped in try/finally. DECISION (the two ACs conflict as written): AC1 wants the claim inside the same $transaction as the reservation, but AC2 wants the loser to touch NO chain state — and the auto-recall, which WRITES to chain, runs between them. Reserving before recalling was rejected because freeTreasuryBalance is balance minus RESERVED rows, so a reservation written first makes recallForPayment over-redeem from the MMF (the 'recall before reserve' invariant is load-bearing). Resolved by splitting: claim first (loser stopped before any chain call, per AC2), then RE-assert the lease inside the reservation's prisma.$transaction, so {lease, reservation} stays atomic — a reservation can never exist without the lease that authorized it. Lease release: transitionStatus clears it on any LEASE_RELEASE_STATES status (new in lib/state.ts = TERMINAL_STATES + FAILED; FAILED is deliberately not terminal since FAILED->REFUNDED is legal — when US-009 adds COMPENSATED to TERMINAL_STATES the lease set follows for free), and the executor's finally is the backstop for throws that never reach a transition (unquoted payment, RPC down during setup) — scoped to its OWN leaseId so it can never free a later attempt's. ExecutionLeaseError extends ApiError('conflict'), so the execute route's existing fromThrown renders the 409 with zero mapping code (same payoff US-006 got from StaleTransitionError). Tests: tests/integration/execution-lease.test.ts (6) — the race asserts ON CHAIN (treasury USDC delta == exactly one payment's amount) rather than only counting audit rows, plus the route-level 200/409 pair, lease-cleared-at-SETTLED, lease-cleared-at-FAILED, lease-released-on-setup-throw, and a held lease refusing a second attempt. Suite 191 -> 197, tsc + lint green. No UI change, so no browser pass.

userStories.title: Idempotency keys for write endpoints
userStories.description: As an API consumer, I want to retry a write safely so that network retries cannot double-create or double-execute.
acceptanceCriteria: IdempotencyRecord prisma model: key (unique per principal), route, requestHash, responseStatus, responseBody, createdAt
POST /api/payments and POST /api/payments/[id]/execute honor an Idempotency-Key header: same key + same request body replays the stored response; same key + different body returns 422
Records expire after 24h (checked at read time — no cron needed)
Integration tests: duplicate create with same key returns the same payment_id and creates one row; conflicting body 422s
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Done 2026-07-16. lib/idempotency.ts (framework-free: beginIdempotent/completeIdempotent/abandonIdempotent, hashRequest, IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_MS) + app/api/idempotency.ts (the NextResponse half — beginIdempotency returns an IdempotentScope OR the response to return, the same narrowing convention guard.ts established). DECISION: reserve-then-stamp, not check-then-write — the first request CREATES the record and the unique index on (principalId, key) decides the race, then stamps the response onto the row it owns; a check-then-write lets two duplicates both pass the check. So a duplicate always finds a row: unstamped -> 409 in_flight, stamped -> replay, different body/route -> 422. Principal gained `keyId` (= ApiKey.id) because 'unique per principal' needs a stable caller identity and Principal had none; principalForKey is the only constructor, so the blast radius was 2 exact-equality assertions in tests/db/auth.test.ts. The scope wraps the WHOLE handler (both routes' bodies extracted to createPayment()/runExecute()), so a retry replays whatever the first call answered including its errors; only a THROW abandons the key, since an unknown outcome must stay retryable while a definite one (even a 409/500) is the answer. `route` is the CONCRETE path ('POST /api/payments/pay_x/execute'), so one key aimed at two payments is a 422 rather than a wrong replay. hashRequest canonicalizes (recursive key sort) because JSON.stringify order is insertion order, which a client does not control. Expiry is reclaim-in-place via a CAS on the row's own createdAt (updateMany where {id, createdAt}), so two concurrent reclaimers cannot both own the key; the begin loop runs at most 2 passes (the row can be abandoned or reclaimed under us). New error code idempotency_conflict -> 422. No FK on principalId: npm run setup drops ApiKey rows and an orphan is harmless. Tests: tests/integration/idempotency.test.ts (10) — replay/one-row, key-order independence, 422 different body, distinct+absent keys, per-principal scoping, 409 in-flight, 24h expiry reuse, oversized key, plus execute replay and cross-payment 422. Suite 197 -> 208, tsc + lint green. No UI change (the demo sends no key and is unaffected), so no browser pass.

userStories.title: Compensation saga for destination-leg failure after source settlement
userStories.description: As a sender, I want my funds compensated if the payout leg fails after escrow was already released to treasury, instead of the payment just being marked FAILED.
acceptanceCriteria: New lifecycle statuses in lib/state.ts: COMPENSATION_PENDING (reachable from PAYOUT_PENDING) and COMPENSATED (terminal, from COMPENSATION_PENDING), enforced by assertTransition; state-machine unit tests updated

Executor: if the destination payout or ledger-credit step throws AFTER settlePayment succeeded, do NOT call failAndRefund (escrow is already released); instead transition to COMPENSATION_PENDING, send a treasury-funded transfer of the source asset amount back to the sender wallet on the source network, then transition to COMPENSATED
Every compensation step audited (tx hashes as strings, never bigint, in audit detail — AGENTS.md gotcha)

Liquidity reservation released; integration test forces a destination failure after settlement (injectable test-only failure hook in the executor) and asserts the sender's source-asset balance is restored
Reconcile on-chain facts before compensating: read the escrow contract's payment status to confirm SETTLED on-chain rather than trusting the DB alone
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Done 2026-07-16. lib/state.ts gains COMPENSATION_PENDING + COMPENSATED (terminal, so LEASE_RELEASE_STATES picked it up for free per US-007's note); lib/chain.ts gains getPayment in SETTLEMENT_ABI + onchainPaymentState(); lib/executor.ts gains compensateSender() and a chain-reconciled catch; Payment gains compensationTxHash. DECISION: the catch now decides refund-vs-compensate by READING THE CHAIN (AC5), not by the DB status list — the DB records what an attempt TRIED, the escrow records what LANDED, and they disagree exactly when a step threw mid-flight, which is the only time this path runs. The old status list survives only as a fallback for when the read itself fails (RPC down). CONSEQUENCE (deviates from AC1's letter): COMPENSATION_PENDING is reachable from CONFIRMED_ONCHAIN and FX_OR_SWAP_COMPLETED as well as PAYOUT_PENDING — if the settle tx lands but its receipt read times out, the DB sits at CONFIRMED_ONCHAIN while the escrow reads SETTLED, and with only the AC's edge transitionStatus would throw 'invalid transition' from inside the catch and the sender would never be compensated. The state machine covers every status where the escrow MAY be released; the chain read picks which applies. Compensation pays the SOURCE asset on the SOURCE network in the exact base units escrowed (amountUnits hoisted out of the try) — the destination leg is what failed, so paying that back would be a bug; the cross-chain test asserts it. A compensation transfer that itself fails leaves the payment in COMPENSATION_PENDING (audited payment.compensation_failed), never FAILED — that would claim the sender was made whole; it is the state US-010 repairs, and the executor's finally frees the lease so a repair can re-enter. Test hooks: exported executorTestHooks with beforeDestinationPayout (the AC's) AND beforeSettlement — the on-chain refund branch had ZERO coverage and this story changed its guard, so it got a regression test proving a held escrow still refunds and does NOT compensate. Also updated the hardcoded UI status lists (STATUS_STYLES, dashboard pending/failed, detail isTerminalBad, balances pending notIn) — they are literals, not derived from lib/state.ts. Tests: tests/integration/compensation.test.ts (4: sender made exactly whole + escrow really SETTLED on-chain + no refund audit; cross-chain compensates on source with destination untouched; audit detail shape incl. amountUnits-as-string; refund-path regression) + 2 state unit tests. Suite 208 -> 214, tsc + lint green. No browser pass: the only UI surface is a badge/counter for states unreachable without the hook.

userStories.title: Operator repair view for partial settlements
userStories.description: As an operator, I want to see payments stuck in partial states and retry/compensate them so that no payment is silently stranded.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/payments?stuck=true (OPERATOR only) lists payments in COMPENSATION_PENDING or FAILED-with-escrow states, including the on-chain escrow status read live from the source network (degrade gracefully if RPC is down, per AGENTS.md)
POST /api/payments/[id]/repair (OPERATOR only) retries the compensation path for COMPENSATION_PENDING payments, idempotently
Dashboard shows a 'needs attention' count linking to a simple list of stuck payments
Integration test: a payment forced into COMPENSATION_PENDING is repaired to COMPENSATED via the endpoint
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Done 2026-07-16. GET /api/payments?stuck=true (OPERATOR only; a REVIEWER that may read every payment may NOT read this view — it names treasury facts and drives a repair) + POST /api/payments/[id]/repair (OPERATOR only, inside the idempotency scope) + /payments/stuck page + dashboard Needs Attention card counted from the same stuckPayments() the list uses, so the count and the list can never disagree. DECISION: which FAILED payments are 'FAILED-with-escrow' (AC1) cannot be answered from the DB — a FAILED payment is only finished if its escrow refunded — so each candidate's escrow is read LIVE and the filter runs on the chain's answer: COMPENSATION_PENDING always listed, FAILED dropped only when the escrow reads REFUNDED, candidates pre-narrowed by onchainPaymentId != null (a payment that failed before escrow holds nothing). DECISION (degrade, per the public-RPC invariant): an unreadable escrow lists as escrow_state null rather than dropping the row — a flaky RPC must not hide the one payment an operator needs to see; repairCompensation conversely REFUSES on an unreadable escrow (409), since it will not pay treasury funds against an escrow it cannot confirm was released, and the transfer would run on that same dead network anyway. 'Idempotently' = three guards: COMPENSATED returns untouched (never pays twice), the execution-lease CAS admits one of two concurrent repairs (200 + 409), and an Idempotency-Key replays the first answer. Refactor: compensateSender split into the transition + runCompensationTransfer (the repair re-enters the transfer half), and compensationContextFor() now derives amount/network/wallet from the row for BOTH the executor's catch and the repair, so they cannot disagree about what to pay. New hooks beforeCompensationTransfer (a real stuck payment: escrow truly SETTLED, sender truly short) and beforeRefund (the FAILED-with-escrow-INITIATED case). Tests: tests/integration/repair.test.ts (9) — assertions land ON CHAIN (sender balance), not just on row counts. Suite 214 -> 223, tsc + lint green. Browser-verified on a real dev server: forced a genuine COMPENSATION_PENDING, saw the dashboard card ('1 payment holding funds...'), the stuck page (escrow SETTLED pill, diagnosis, Retry compensation button), repaired via the button's endpoint -> COMPENSATED, sender back to 1,000,000 mockUSDC, second repair replayed the same tx hash without paying again, list and card both empty afterwards, audit chain INTACT with the full compensation_pending -> compensation_failed -> compensation_transfer -> compensated trail. GOTCHA: a stale .next/ cache 404'd every API route incl. untouched ones — rm -rf .next (now in AGENTS.md).

userStories.title: Strict canonical decimal validation at the API boundary
userStories.description: As a platform owner, I want malformed or over-precise amounts rejected so that '1e6', 'Infinity', and 25000.001 JPY can never enter the system.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/money.ts: parseAmount(amountStr, currency) accepting only ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ with at most the currency's decimal places (JPY 0, USD/SGD 2), no leading '+', no exponent, max 15 integer digits; returns bigint minor units; throws typed MoneyError otherwise — excess precision is REJECTED, never truncated
POST /api/payments validates amount via parseAmount and stores the canonical string form; invalid input returns 400 invalid_request with a safe message
Unit tests: scientific notation, Infinity, NaN, negative, empty, '25000.001' JPY rejected; '25000.00' USD, '0.01' USD, '100' JPY accepted with correct minor units
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Done 2026-07-16. lib/money.ts is framework-free like api-errors.ts (parseAmount -> bigint minor units, formatMinorUnits, canonicalAmount, currencyDecimals, CURRENCY_DECIMALS, typed MoneyError with codes INVALID_FORMAT/EXCESS_PRECISION/TOO_LARGE/NOT_POSITIVE/UNSUPPORTED_CURRENCY); POST /api/payments maps MoneyError -> invalidRequest(e.message) (safe: the messages are ours, not a thrown internal). parseAmount takes `unknown`, not `string` — it runs on unvalidated bodies where a declared `amount?: string` is a hope, and a JSON number (100000) must be rejected too. NOTE the two decimal notions that now coexist: CURRENCY_DECIMALS is FIAT minor units (USD 2, JPY 0) and is what the boundary validates against; ASSETS[].decimals is TOKEN base units (mockUSDC 6, mockJPY 0) and is what toBaseUnits still uses downstream. They are not the same number for USD/SGD — do not merge them. ROUTE ORDER CHANGED: the currency-support check (CURRENCY_TO_ASSET) now runs BEFORE the amount check, because the source currency is what says how much precision is legal; the old `Number(amount) <= 0 || isNaN` gate is gone (it accepted '1e6' and 'Infinity'). DECISION (strict digit count, per AC1's 'at most the currency's decimal places'): '100000.00' JPY is now a 400 even though the trailing zeros are lossless — 'the string's precision must match the currency' is a cleaner contract than '...unless the extra digits happen to be zero', and it makes canonical form a bijection. That broke ONE pre-existing test (api.test.ts's JPY->JPY same-currency case sent the USD-shaped '100000.00'), updated to '100000'. Demo UI unaffected: app/payments/new defaults to USD->JPY so the source is USD; picking JPY as SOURCE with the default amount now surfaces 'JPY amounts must be whole numbers' in the form's existing error banner, which is the rule working, so the UI was deliberately left alone (silently reformatting the user's typed value is the truncation this story exists to prevent). Payment.amount is now stored canonical ('1234.5' -> '1234.50'), asserted by a new integration test. Tests: tests/unit/money.test.ts (15) + 3 integration cases in api.test.ts (Number()-coercible inputs incl. a JSON number, JPY over-precision, canonical storage). Suite 223 -> 241, tsc + lint green. Left for US-012/US-013: parseAmount is only wired into the create route — fx.ts/routing.ts still do float math, and treasury.ts keeps its own private parseAmount (token decimals, truncating) which is a candidate to fold in during US-013.

userStories.title: FX and fee math on bigint minor units
userStories.description: As a platform owner, I want quoting/fee arithmetic off JS floats so that every quoted figure is exact.

Quote API responses are unchanged in shape (strings); update test fixtures where floor-rounding legitimately shifts the last minor unit and call it out in notes
No Number() arithmetic on monetary values remains in lib/fx.ts (Number allowed only for bps constants and display formatting)
Unit tests: known-rate fixtures assert exact bigint results incl. JPY 0-decimals and a value that would lose precision as a float (> 2^53 minor units)
